Key Activities: Integrates and analyzes statistical outputs and reviews/certifies the quality and completeness of the individual program results.
Develops statistical systems and processes, evaluates the quality of collections’ outputs and prepares analytical reviews.
Evaluates changes in the statistical needs of clients and develops new methods of collecting, coding and processing data.
Provides advice and guidance to users on the development, operation and use of collection systems and processes.
Acts as a divisional data collection and operations representative on projects, task forces or committees in various roles.
Supervises a unit or project team involved in the development of collection procedures and the capture, coding and processing of statistical data.

1. Decision making: Investigates client requirements for statistical information, determines the sources of information, methods and approaches to be used for the collection, capture, coding and processing of data. Modifies existing techniques, methods and approaches or develops new ones to meet specific needs. Each statistical project is unique in nature and decisions impact on other statistical programs.

Defines project objectives and priorities and assesses the requirements to conduct developmental projects; prepares work plans and summaries outlining approaches, time-frames and resources involved in the operation of statistical systems and processes.
Proposes modifications to program content and coverage and operational procedures, such as new or modified data sources, concepts, methods and definitions.

Evaluates the effectiveness of existing and new statistical systems and processes, the quality and completeness of outputs and pepares studies and reports for use by senior management of the division in assessing the attainment of divisional program objectives and the cost, efficiency and utilization of divisional resources.

Develops and distributes guidelines, instructions and procedures for the development, use and evaluation of statistical systems and processes for use by operational and systems staff when planning and performing their work.
Establishes and implements specifications, guidelines and procedures for the maintenance and safeguarding of computer systems, equipment, databases and files.

Develops proposals and recommends changes and improvements on questionnaire design, enhancements or modifications to survey content and coverage, revisions to collection or production systems and processes, and the implementation of new hardware and software to be used in data collection or statistical production activities.
2. Leadership and operational management: Supervises a unit involved in statistical operations and/or leads project teams for special projects. Determines goals, priorities and milestones, sets objectives, and plans and schedules the work, resolves conflicting priorities; identifies human resources needs, determines the appropriate selection methods (internal and external resources / contractors) to meet program or project objectives, recruits staff, evaluates employee performance, develops training plans, motivates and maintains morale of employees.

Plans and budgets for on-going operations and/or special projects, including estimates for salaries, professional fees and implementation costs, with authority to allocate/reallocate funds within the budget. Provides input to budgets based on operational needs and by obtaining/providing cost estimates for personnel, supplies, equipment purchases and travel for use in developing section or division budgets. Establishes and negotiates contracts for projects. Responsible for the acquisition of goods and services, according to the budget allocated.
3. Communication: Provides advice and interpretation to various data users at all levels of government, business and national social agencies and academics, on the practical use and application of statistical data and information. This often requires the adaptation and presentation of complex information in basic, understandable formats. When media representatives and others challenge or misinterpret findings, it is necessary to further explain the results and statistical methods and approaches used in order to maintain the department’s reputation for producing high quality data.
Writes and presents subject matter and technical concepts, definitions and terms in common terminology in order to explain and clarify operational systems and processes or explain program results.
Prepares and explains specifications and guidelines to be used by others in developing and operating systems and processes.
Chairs intra-departmental meetings and participates in inter-departmental meetings, conferences and groups to develop consensus or share knowledge within the area of operational expertise.
4. Knowledge of specialized fields: Knowledge of economic/sociology principles and practices as they relate to a specialized area as well as specific knowledge of the area to initiate and conduct projects to improve existing concepts or to develop new approaches to extend processing systems applications for the collection, capture, coding and processing of statistical data. This knowledge is also required to provide expert advice and guidance to users within and outside Statistics Canada.
Knowledge of statistical theories, methods (including data gathering and analysis techniques), concepts and practices used in the collection, capture, coding and processing of statistical data.
Knowledge of the principles and practices of human and financial resource management is required to manage the work of a multi-disciplinary unit and/or a project team.
5. Contextual knowledge: Knowledge of the departmental and divisional mandate, objectives and organization is required in the management of statistical operations.
Knowledge of Statistics Canada policies, practices and classification systems is needed to ensure that they are applied in the conduct of statistical projects and activities.
Knowledge of other statistical programs related to the area of expertise within the department, especially the concepts, methods, and databases used in other divisions.

Knowledge of departmental publication, marketing and dissemination policies and practices in order to establish common divisional policies and practices in the preparation of statistical tables, charts, explanatory notes etc. for dissemination to user and/or subject matter clients.

Knowledge of data suppliers is required to discuss data reporting agreements, as well as knowledge of data users from governments and the private sector to identify potential new markets, to understand client needs for complex statistical data or studies, to negotiate contracts and to provide advice on survey results.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act and other pertinent acts such as the Corporate Returns Act and Income Tax Act, and of Statistics Canada policies to explain legislative and policy requirements to data suppliers, users and others with respect to the collection, capture, coding and processing of data. Knowledge of the Statitstics and Privacy Acts is particulary important with respect to the security and confidentiality of information and data provided and to ensure that they and their subordinates do not release any information which may identify an individual or group without prior consent.
6. Research and analysis: Interprets the relative quality of data produced, determines reasons for variances, its comparability over time and its relevancy in light of changing requirements, trends, developments, policy issues and socio-economic conditions.

Reviews and modifies existing operational techniques, methods and approaches or develops new ones to meet specific needs. Operational programs may involve a combination of statistical techniques and methods and the integration of data from a variety of sources (e.g. financial statements, tax files, other administrative sources, surveys, censuses). Often, the data have often been collected for other purposes using different definitions or concepts and must be translated into common concepts.

Reviews and resolves gaps and inconsistencies in the collection, capture, coding and processing methods and procedures used, reviews the conceptual framework used and the compatibility with other statistical programs, reviews and resolves technical and conceptual problems referred by staff or project teams.

Analysis is required to understand and interpret user requirements for statistical information and translate them into a concrete, timely and affordable information request. Clients are often uncertain of their data needs and are unfamiliar with statistical options, methods and techniques available.

Job Poster.Assets: Essential qualifications English essential EDUCATION: Successful completion of two years of post secondary education with acceptable specialization in social science, statistics, library/archival work or a law related field, or acceptable combination of education, training and/or experience. EXPERIENCE: Experience developing processes and procedures related to collection activities of large-scale operations such as Census; Experience developing processes and procedures related to staff management and supervision; Experience managing staff in production or call centre environments; Experience in project management and use of project management tools; Experience supervising decentralized teams; Experience interacting with service areas and divisional personnel to resolve planning, development and production issues. COMPETENCIES: Demonstrating integrity and respect; Thinking things through; Working effectively with others; Showing initiative and being action oriented. ABILITIES: Ability to communicate effectively orally and in writing; Ability to manage competing priorities; Ability to identify and resolve problems.
Job Poster.Area of Selection: Employees of Statistics Canada occupying a position within the Census Operations Division in the Ottawa region.
